drug_class: Antifibrinolytic agent (a medicine that helps stop bleeding)
purpose: Tranexamic acid is used to help control or reduce heavy bleeding. It is commonly prescribed for women with heavy menstrual periods, and it is also used to prevent or treat bleeding during surgery or after an injury. Think of it as a medicine that helps your body form and keep blood clots where they are needed.
how_it_works: Normally, your body makes clots to stop bleeding, but it also has a system that breaks those clots down. Tranexamic acid works by blocking the process that dissolves blood clots, so the clots stay in place longer and bleeding slows down or stops. It does not actually make new clots — it just helps the ones you already have do their job better.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or an upset stomach. Some people also experience headache, back pain, muscle aches, or fatigue. These side effects are usually mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of forming dangerous blood clots in your legs, lungs, or brain, especially if you already have a history of clotting problems or are taking hormonal birth control. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, as the dose may need to be adjusted. Do not use this medicine if you have active blood clots. Seek emergency help right away if you notice sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, leg swelling, or vision changes.
typical_dosing: For heavy periods, the typical dose is 1,300 mg (two 650 mg tablets) taken by mouth three times a day for up to 5 days during your menstrual period. For other uses like surgery, dosing is determined by your doctor and may be given as an injection. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your situation.
